The mechanism is grounded in the diff; I cannot fully confirm runtime duplication without more context, so confidence is moderate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept `(event, credentialId)` and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination. In `CalendarManager.createEvent`, the only value forwarded to the calendar integration is `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (the `externalId` is not passed through). GoogleCalendarService uses the new `credentialId` param to select the matching destination calendar (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and the shared `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` all derive `calendarId` from the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and do not use `credentialId` to pick the correct destination. With multiple destination calendars (e.g., collective/team destinations pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar`), each credential-specific create call will still target destinationCalendar[0], causing duplicate inserts into the main host calendar and missing events on teammates’ calendars.
